passage:
Zeenat: Mehak, can we talk for five minutes? Just us, by the gate.
Mehak: Sure. Is it about the maths thing?
Zeenat: Sort of. When I heard the whole bench knew I still sleep with the hall light on, I felt small. I only told you.
Mehak: I didn't think...
Zeenat: I'm not saying you're a bad friend. I felt really embarrassed, and I want to understand what happened.
Mehak: Ritu asked why you skipped the sleepover and I said too much. I thought it was funny. I'm sorry.
Zeenat: Thanks for telling me. Next time, can you ask me first?
Mehak: Yes. I should have. Want to get chai? 🙂

qa.q: Where did Zeenat ask to talk to Mehak?
qa.a: Zeenat asked to talk just the two of them, by the gate.

qa.q: How does Zeenat feel about the hall light becoming known?
qa.a: Zeenat feels small and embarrassed, because Zeenat only told Mehak.

qa.q: What could Zeenat try if Mehak became defensive, and why?
qa.a: Zeenat could write a short note explaining the hurt and give Mehak time to think, because reading in private can lower defensiveness.

qa.q: How does the conversation look to Mehak?
qa.a: Mehak feels guilty and sorry but not attacked, because Zeenat says 'I felt' and asks what happened instead of accusing.

grounding: The student asks for a one-to-one talk, says how it felt when the secret spread, and asks what happened, naming feelings without accusing.

passage: I'm Pooja, and last year Chaitanya told half our class that I still slept with a night light. I had told only Chaitanya. For two days I avoided the whole group. Then I asked, "Can we talk after school? Just us?" We sat on the low wall behind the basketball court. I had practised the first line. "When I heard everyone knew about the night light, I felt embarrassed, and really hurt, because I'd only told you." I didn't say "you always" or "you're such a gossip", though I wanted to. Then I asked, "What happened?" Chaitanya went red and said it had slipped out when someone was joking about ghosts, and had felt awful afterwards. We both went quiet. Then Chaitanya said sorry, properly, without a "but".

qa.q: Where did Pooja and Chaitanya talk?
qa.a: On the low wall behind the basketball court.

qa.q: What was Pooja feeling on hearing that everyone knew?
qa.a: Pooja felt embarrassed and deeply hurt, because the secret had been shared with only Chaitanya.

qa.q: Why did Pooja's first line work better than calling Chaitanya a gossip?
qa.a: It named Pooja's own feelings without attacking, so Chaitanya could listen and explain instead of getting defensive.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya have felt during the talk?
qa.a: Chaitanya seems ashamed, going red and admitting it felt awful, and eased enough by the calm tone to apologise properly.

grounding: A student recalls asking a friend to talk alone and naming feelings about a spread secret without accusing, so the friend didn't get defensive.

passage:
Counsellor's note, 9 August — Gautam, Class 10
Gautam came to see me on Monday. His best friend Neeraj had told the football team that Gautam was afraid of deep water, something Gautam had shared in confidence. He wanted to "have it out" in front of everyone. We talked about what he actually wanted, and he said, "For him to get why it mattered." So we practised. Today I saw them on the bench by the office after school, just the two of them. From the door I heard Gautam say, "I felt stupid when the team found out. I'd only told you." Then, "What happened?" Neeraj's shoulders, which had been up by his ears, came down. They talked for about twenty minutes. Afterwards both came in to borrow the football, together. I will check in with Gautam on Friday.
— Vijay

qa.q: What had Gautam shared with Neeraj in confidence?
qa.a: That Gautam was afraid of deep water.

qa.q: What did Gautam feel when the team found out?
qa.a: He felt stupid and embarrassed, and hurt because he had told only Neeraj.

qa.q: Why did talking privately work better than having it out in front of everyone?
qa.a: In private Neeraj could listen without losing face, and the I-statements let him relax instead of defending himself.

qa.q: How did Neeraj seem to react to Gautam's words?
qa.a: His raised shoulders came down, suggesting he went from tense and defensive to calmer and willing to talk.

grounding: A counsellor's note shows a student talking one-to-one with a friend, using I-statements about a spread secret, which kept the friend from getting defensive.
